text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Aides to prime minister predict no indictment.
- Public Security Minister Avigdor Kahalani: Government won't survive if prime minister indicted.
- Former Israeli president Chaim Herzog dies.
- January/February Tel Aviv stock exchange foreign investments rose 23 percent; Israelis invested 15 billion shekels over same period overseas.
- Central bank, Treasury leave currency basket intact.
- Insurance cartel let down industry, Finance Minister Dan Meridor says.
- Meridor: Lessons must be learned from insurance cartel affair.
- Udi Recanati: "We did not make nor are we making contacts to buy Discount Bank".

- Netanyahu: The truth will triumph. Expectation: No indictments against Netanyahu, Hanegbi and Lieberman. Doubts about Deri. Coalition: Even a serious report would force Yisrael ba-Aliya and Third Way out of the government. Opposition plans demonstration in Rabin Square under the banner: Bibi Go Home.
- Poll: 52 percent believe police acted professionally.
- Netanyahu: I'll not quit. Signs of crisis in government.
